adds.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (amended 1991, 2006)
adds.summary: New Jersey's Law Against Discrimination was amended in 1991 to prohibit discrimination based on affectional or sexual orientation and in 2006 to prohibit discrimination based on gender identity or expression. For trans visitors this bars denial of goods, services, facilities or lodging based on gender identity or expression in places of public accommodation including hotels, restaurants, stores and transportation and in housing, enforceable through complaints to the Division on Civil Rights for investigation and relief.

adds.title: 2018 transgender rights package - birth certificates, death certificates, Transgender Equality Task Force
adds.summary: On July 3, 2018 Governor Murphy signed the Babs Siperstein Law removing the proof-of-surgery requirement for changing gender marker on New Jersey birth certificates and creating a nonbinary third-gender option, making New Jersey the 17th state to allow surgery-free changes and the fourth state with a third birth-certificate option after California, Oregon and Washington, and also signed companion measures allowing gender identity to be reflected on death certificates and establishing a Transgender Task Force of government officials, law/policy/medical experts and community advocates to study issues affecting transgender people.
